'''Karen Vogtmann''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}} (born July 13, 1949 in [[Pittsburg, California]]<ref name="N02">[https://www.ams.org/notices/200208/bios02.pdf ''Biographies of Candidates 2002.''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220115153622/https://www.ams.org/notices/200208/bios02.pdf |date=January 15, 2022 }} [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]. September  2002,  Volume 49,  Issue 8, pp. 970–981</ref>) is an American mathematician working primarily in the area of [[geometric group theory]]. She introduced, in a 1986 paper with [[Marc Culler]],<ref name="CV86">{{Citation | last1 = Culler | first1 = Marc | last2 = Vogtmann | first2 = Karen | title = Moduli of graphs and automorphisms of free groups | journal = [[Inventiones Mathematicae]] | volume = 84 | issue = 1 | pages = 91–119 | year = 1986 | url = https://www.math.cornell.edu/~vogtmann/ScannedPapers/1986.0084.pdf | doi = 10.1007/BF01388734 | postscript = . | bibcode = 1986InMat..84...91C | s2cid = 122869546 | access-date = November 29, 2008 | archive-date = June 12, 2007 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20070612192601/http://www.math.cornell.edu/~vogtmann/ScannedPapers/1986.0084.pdf | url-status = live }}</ref> an object now known as the [[Culler–Vogtmann Outer space]]. The Outer space is a [[free group]] analog of the [[Teichmüller space]] of a [[Riemann surface]] and is particularly useful in the study of the [[group (mathematics)|group]] of [[outer automorphism]]s of the free group on ''n'' generators, [[Out(Fn)|Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>)]]. Vogtmann is a professor of mathematics at [[Cornell University]] and the [[University of Warwick]].

==Biographical data==
Vogtmann was inspired to pursue mathematics by a [[National Science Foundation]] summer program for high school students at the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="AWM"/>

She received a B.A. from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1971. Vogtmann then obtained a PhD in mathematics, also from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1977.<ref name="N07">[https://www.ams.org/notices/200708/tx070801043p.pdf ''Biographies of Candidates 2007.''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090902104456/http://www.ams.org/notices/200708/tx070801043p.pdf |date=September 2, 2009 }} [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]. September  2007,  Volume 54,  Issue 8, pp. 1043–1057</ref> Her PhD advisor was John Wagoner and her doctoral thesis was on [[algebraic K-theory]].<ref name="AWM">[http://www.awm-math.org/noetherbrochure/Vogtmann07.html Karen Vogtmann] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161022201834/http://www.awm-math.org/noetherbrochure/Vogtmann07.html |date=2016-10-22 }}, 2007 [[Noether Lecture]], Profiles of Women in Mathematics. The Emmy Noether Lectures. [[Association for Women in Mathematics]]. Accessed November 28, 2008</ref>

She then held positions at [[University of Michigan]], [[Brandeis University]] and [[Columbia University]].<ref name=CV/> Vogtmann has been a faculty member at [[Cornell University]] since 1984, and she became a full professor at Cornell in 1994.<ref name=CV/>  In September 2013, she also joined the [[University of Warwick]]. She is married to the mathematician [[John David Smillie|John Smillie]]. The couple moved in 2013 to England and settled in [[Kenilworth]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Obituary {{!}} Anna K. Smillie (1929–2020)|website=Cremation Society of the Carolinas|url=https://www.cremnc.com/obituary/anna-smillie|access-date=August 21, 2021|archive-date=August 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210821130335/https://www.cremnc.com/obituary/anna-smillie|url-status=live}}</ref> She is currently a professor of mathematics at Warwick, and a Goldwin Smith Professor of Mathematics Emeritus at Cornell.<ref name=CV/>

Vogtmann has been the vice-president of the [[American Mathematical Society]] (2003–2006).<ref name="N07"/><ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200302/from-elections.pdf 2002 Election results.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220310051149/http://www.ams.org/notices/200302/from-elections.pdf |date=March 10, 2022 }} [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]. February 2003, Volume 50  Issue 2, p. 281</ref> She has been elected to serve as a member of the board of trustees of the American Mathematical Society for the period February 2008 – January 2018.<ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/200802/tx080200301p.pdf 2007 Election Results.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220310051152/http://www.ams.org/notices/200802/tx080200301p.pdf |date=March 10, 2022 }} [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]. February 2008, Volume 55, Issue 2, p. 301</ref><ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/201302/rnoti-p256.pdf 2012 Election Results] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230329164142/https://www.ams.org/notices/201302/rnoti-p256.pdf |date=March 29, 2023 }}, [[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]], February 2013, Volume 60, Issue 2, p. 256</ref>

Vogtmann is a former editorial board member (2006–2016) of the journal ''[[Algebraic and Geometric Topology]]''  and a former associate editor of ''[[Bulletin of the American Mathematical Society]]''.<ref name=CV>[http://homepages.warwick.ac.uk/~masmbe/VitaeWarwick.html CURRICULUM VITAE - Karen Vogtmann] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190403123647/http://homepages.warwick.ac.uk/~masmbe/VitaeWarwick.html |date=April 3, 2019 }}, [[University of Warwick]]. Accessed September 14, 2017</ref> 
She is currently an associate editor of the ''[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]'',<ref>[https://www.ams.org/publications/journals/journalsframework/jamsedit editorial board] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210413221146/https://www.ams.org/publications/journals/journalsframework/jamsedit |date=April 13, 2021 }}, ''[[Journal of the American Mathematical Society]]''. Accessed September 14, 2017.</ref> an editorial board member  ''Geometry & Topology Monographs'' book series,<ref>[https://msp.org/gtm/about/journal/manag.html editorial board] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170914173321/https://msp.org/gtm/about/journal/manag.html |date=September 14, 2017 }}, ''Geometry & Topology Monographs''. Accessed September 14, 2017</ref> and a consulting editor for the ''[[Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society]]''.<ref>[https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/proceedings-of-the-edinburgh-mathematical-society/information/editorial-board editorial board] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191217031330/https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/proceedings-of-the-edinburgh-mathematical-society/information/editorial-board |date=December 17, 2019 }}, ''[[Proceedings of the Edinburgh Mathematical Society]]''. She is also a member of the [[ArXiv]] advisory board.<ref>[https://arxiv.org/ad-board.html ArXiv Advisory Board.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100612190118/http://arxiv.org/ad-board.html |date=June 12, 2010 }} [[ArXiv]]. Accessed November 27, 2008</ref>

Since 1986 Vogtmann has been a co-organizer of the annual conference called the ''Cornell Topology Festival''<ref>[https://vivo.cornell.edu/individual/vivo/individual28265 Cornell Topology Festival, grant summary.] [[Cornell University]]. Accessed November 28, 2008</ref> that usually takes places at [[Cornell University]] each May.

==Mathematical contributions==
Vogtmann's early work concerned [[Homology (mathematics)|homological]] properties of [[orthogonal group]]s associated to [[quadratic form]]s over various [[field (mathematics)|fields]].<ref>Karen Vogtmann, [https://www.math.cornell.edu/~vogtmann/ScannedPapers/1981.0020.pdf ''Spherical posets and homology stability for <math>O_{n,n}</math>''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170215070126/http://www.math.cornell.edu/~vogtmann/ScannedPapers/1981.0020.pdf |date=February 15, 2017 }} [[Topology (journal)|Topology]], vol. 20 (1981), no. 2, pp. 119–132.</ref><ref>Karen Vogtmann, [https://www.math.cornell.edu/~vogtmann/ScannedPapers/1982.0057.pdf ''A Stiefel complex for the orthogonal group of a field''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160303201001/http://www.math.cornell.edu/~vogtmann/ScannedPapers/1982.0057.pdf |date=March 3, 2016 }} [[Commentarii Mathematici Helvetici]], vol. 57 (1982), no. 1, pp. 11–21</ref>

Vogtmann's most important contribution came in a 1986 paper with Marc Culler called "Moduli of graphs and automorphisms of free groups".<ref name="CV86"/> The paper introduced an object that came to be known as [[Culler–Vogtmann Outer space]]. The Outer space ''X<sub>n</sub>'', associated to a [[free group]] ''F''<sub>''n''</sub>, is a free group analog<ref>{{Cite book |last=Farb |first=Benson |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=uiqDbaQRr7IC&dq=%22outer+space%22+vogtmann&pg=PA335 |title=Problems on Mapping Class Groups and Related Topics |date=12 September 2006 |publisher=American Mathematical Soc. |isbn=978-0-8218-3838-9 |page=335}}</ref> of the [[Teichmüller space]] of a [[Riemann surface]]. Instead of marked [[conformal structure]]s (or, in an equivalent model, hyperbolic structures) on a surface, points of the Outer space are represented by volume-one ''marked metric graphs''. A ''marked metric graph'' consists of a [[homotopy equivalence]] between a [[wedge sum|wedge]] of ''n'' circles and a finite connected graph ''Γ'' without degree-one and degree-two vertices, where ''Γ'' is equipped with a volume-one metric structure, that is, assignment of positive real lengths to edges of ''Γ'' so that the sum of the lengths of all edges is equal to one. Points of ''X<sub>n</sub>'' can also be thought of as free and discrete minimal isometric actions ''F''<sub>''n''</sub> on [[real tree]]s where the quotient graph has volume one.

By construction the Outer space ''X<sub>n</sub>'' is a finite-dimensional [[simplicial complex]] equipped with a natural action of [[Out(Fn)|Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>)]] which is properly discontinuous and has finite simplex stabilizers. The main result of Culler–Vogtmann 1986 paper,<ref name="CV86"/> obtained via Morse-theoretic methods, was that the Outer space ''X<sub>n</sub>'' is contractible. Thus the [[Quotient space (topology)|quotient space]] ''X<sub>n</sub>'' /Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>) is "almost" a [[classifying space]] for [[Out(Fn)|Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>)]] and it can be thought of as a classifying space over '''[[Rational number|Q]]'''. Moreover, Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>) is known to be [[virtually]] torsion-free, so for any torsion-free [[subgroup]] ''H'' of Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>) the action of ''H'' on ''X<sub>n</sub>'' is discrete and free, so that ''X<sub>n</sub>''/''H'' is a classifying space for ''H''. For these reasons the Outer space is a particularly useful object in obtaining [[homology (mathematics)|homological]] and [[cohomology|cohomological]] information about Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>). In particular, Culler and Vogtmann proved<ref name="CV86"/> that Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>) has virtual cohomological dimension 2''n''&nbsp;−&nbsp;3.

In their 1986 paper Culler and Vogtmann do not assign ''X<sub>n</sub>'' a specific name. According to Vogtmann,<ref>Karen Vogtmann, [https://doi.org/10.1023%2FA%3A1020973910646 ''Automorphisms of free groups and Outer space''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240524152053/https://link.springer.com/article/10.1023/A:1020973910646 |date=May 24, 2024 }}  [[Geometriae Dedicata]], vol. 94 (2002), pp. 1–31; Quote from p. 3: "Peter Shalen later invented the name ''Outer space'' for ''X<sub>n</sub>''".</ref> the term ''Outer space'' for the complex ''X<sub>n</sub>'' was later coined by [[Peter Shalen]]. In subsequent years the Outer space became a central object in the study of [[Out(Fn)|Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>)]]. In particular, the Outer space has a natural compactification, similar to [[William Thurston|Thurston]]'s compactification of the [[Teichmüller space]], and studying the action of Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>) on this compactification yields interesting information about dynamical properties of [[automorphism]]s of [[free group]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Bestvina |first1=M. |author-link=Mladen Bestvina |last2=Feighn |first2=M. |last3=Handel |first3=M. |date=1997 |title=Laminations, trees, and irreducible automorphisms of free groups |journal=Geometric and Functional Analysis |volume=7 |issue=2 |pages=215–244 |doi=10.1007/PL00001618}}</ref><ref name="LL03">Gilbert Levitt and Martin Lustig, ''Irreducible automorphisms of F<sub>n</sub> have north-south dynamics on compactified Outer space.'' Journal of the Institute of Mathematics of Jussieu, vol. 2  (2003),  no. 1, 59–72</ref><ref>{{citation|first1=Gilbert|last1=Levitt|first2=Martin|last2=Lustig|doi=10.1515/CRELLE.2008.038|title=Automorphisms of free groups have asymptotically periodic dynamics|journal=[[Crelle's Journal]]|volume=2008|year=2008|issue=619 |pages=1–36|arxiv=math/0407437}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal | url=http://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0012959300001178 | doi=10.1016/S0012-9593(00)00117-8 | title=Dynamics of Out(Fn) on the boundary of outer space | journal=Annales Scientifiques de l'École Normale Supérieure | date=May 2000 | volume=33 | issue=4 | pages=433–465 | last1=Guirardel | first1=Vincent }}</ref>

Much of Vogtmann's subsequent work concerned the study of the Outer space ''X<sub>n</sub>'', particularly its homotopy, homological and cohomological properties, and related questions for Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>). For example, Hatcher and Vogtmann<ref>{{cite journal | url=http://journals.cambridge.org/action/displayAbstract;jsessionid=753CA10194DFA78D4CD7F09A54C6CD38.tomcat1?fromPage=online&aid=20197 | doi=10.1112/S0024610798006644 | title=Cerf Theory for Graphs | date=1998 | last1=Hatcher | first1=Allen | last2=Vogtmann | first2=Karen | journal=Journal of the London Mathematical Society | volume=58 | issue=3 | pages=633–655 | url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hatcher |first1=A. |last2=Vogtmann |first2=K. |date=2004 |title=Homology stability for outer automorphism groups of free groups |url=http://www.emis.de/journals/UW/agt/ftp/main/2004/agt-4l54.pdf |journal=Algebraic and Geometric Topology |volume=4 |issue=2 |pages=1253–1272|doi=10.2140/agt.2004.4.1253 }}</ref> obtained a number of homological stability results for Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>) and Aut(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>).

In her papers with Conant,<ref>James Conant, and Karen Vogtmann.
[http://www.emis.de/journals/UW/agt/ftp/main/2003/agt-3-42.pdf ''On a theorem of Kontsevich''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220125035858/http://www.emis.de/journals/UW/agt/ftp/main/2003/agt-3-42.pdf |date=January 25, 2022 }} Algebraic and Geometric Topology, vol. 3 (2003), pp. 1167–1224</ref><ref>{{cite journal | doi=10.1007/s00208-003-0465-2 | title=Infinitesimal operations on complexes of graphs | date=2003 | last1=Conant | first1=Jim | last2=Vogtmann | first2=Karen | journal=Mathematische Annalen | volume=327 | issue=3 | pages=545–573 | arxiv=math/0111198 }}</ref><ref>James Conant, and Karen Vogtmann, [http://www.emis.de/journals/GT/ftp/main/2004/2004l40.pdf ''Morita classes in the homology of automorphism groups of free groups.''] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220429054700/https://www.emis.de/journals/GT/ftp/main/2004/2004l40.pdf |date=April 29, 2022 }} [[Geometry & Topology]], vol. 8 (2004), pp. 1471–1499</ref> Vogtmann explored the connection found by [[Maxim Kontsevich]] between the cohomology of certain infinite-dimensional [[Lie algebra]]s and the homology of Out(''F''<sub>''n''</sub>).

A 2001 paper of Vogtmann, joint with [[Louis Billera]] and [[Susan P. Holmes]], used the ideas of [[geometric group theory]] and [[CAT(0) space|CAT(0) geometry]] to study the space of [[phylogenetic tree]]s, that is trees showing possible evolutionary relationships between different species.<ref>{{cite journal | last1=Billera | first1=Louis J. | author1-link=Louis Billera | last2=Holmes | first2=Susan P. | author2-link=Susan P. Holmes | last3=Vogtmann | first3=Karen | author3-link=Karen Vogtmann | title=A Grove of Evolutionary Trees | url=http://www.sciencenews.org/view/generic/id/8501/title/Math_Trek__A_Grove_of_Evolutionary_Trees | year=2001 | journal=[[Advances in Applied Mathematics]] | volume=27 | issue=4 | pages=733–767 | doi=10.1006/aama.2001.0759 | mr=1867931 | access-date=November 29, 2008 | archive-date=February 27, 2012 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120227192626/http://www.sciencenews.org/view/generic/id/8501/title/Math_Trek__A_Grove_of_Evolutionary_Trees }}</ref>  Identifying precise evolutionary trees is an important basic problem in [[mathematical biology]] and one also needs to have good quantitative tools for estimating how accurate a particular evolutionary tree is. The paper of Billera, Vogtmann and Holmes produced a method for quantifying the difference between two evolutionary trees, effectively determining the distance between them.<ref name="JR">Julie Rehmeyer. [http://www.sciencenews.org/view/generic/id/8501/title/Math_Trek__A_Grove_of_Evolutionary_Trees ''A Grove of Evolutionary Trees''.] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120227192626/http://www.sciencenews.org/view/generic/id/8501/title/Math_Trek__A_Grove_of_Evolutionary_Trees |date=February 27, 2012 }} [[Science News]]. May 10, 2007. Accessed November 28, 2008</ref> The fact that the space of [[phylogenetic tree]]s has "non-positively curved geometry", particularly the uniqueness of shortest paths or ''geodesics'' in [[CAT(0) space]]s, allows using these results for practical statistical computations of estimating the confidence level of how accurate particular evolutionary tree is. A free software package implementing these algorithms has been developed and is actively used by biologists.<ref name="JR"/>
